content: Giant manta rays can grow up to nine meters (30 feet) long with a disk size of seven meters (23 feet) across and weigh up to 2,000 kg (4,400 pounds). This size leaves them with very few natural enemies once they reach adulthood at around eight to 10 years old. But giant manta ray babies, called pups, cannot rely on their size to protect them from predators that live in the open ocean, including several species of shark and orcas.
summary: Baby manta ray pups remain close to coastal areas before venturing into the open ocean. Lacking the size of adult mantas, the pups are vulnerable to predators such as sharks and orcas.
author: Phys.org

title: YouTube says it is not testing dislike button hide, but will move it in creator UI
content:
YouTube has denied reports that it is testing a feature to hide the dislike button from users. In a statement to The Verge, spokesperson Kimberly Taylor confirmed that the platform is "not testing hiding the dislike button on YouTube for users." This clarification follows Tuesday’s publication of a story noting that screenshots shared on X appeared to show the button moved into a three-dot menu.

The company stated that it is instead introducing a new user interface for creators on their uploaded videos, where the dislike button will be relocated. Taylor’s full statement emphasized the distinction between user-facing changes and the new design elements intended for content creators.
summary: YouTube spokesperson Kimberly Taylor told The Verge that the platform is not testing hiding the dislike button for users. YouTube is introducing a new creator UI that will move the dislike button into the three‑dot menu on uploaded videos.
author: The Verge

title: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr warns broadcasters against airing “fake polls”
content:
Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr issued a warning to broadcasters on X, cautioning them against airing “fake polls” that have been a frequent target of President Trump’s criticism of the news media. Carr said that many journalists and broadcasters have been “amplifying or airing these polls without regard to basic journalistic ethics and without informing the public that those polls lack a scientific, accurate, or even real basis.” He urged stations to avoid “News Distortions” or “Broadcast Hoaxes” by refraining from airing polls that would violate regulatory obligations and to provide viewers with additional context and information about the polls they cover.

Carr cited recent examples, noting that a small polling outfit was exposed as a hoax this week and a similar incident occurred in August. He pointed out that news outlets have reported on these hoaxes, supplying the context he said is necessary.
summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr warns broadcasters against airing “fake polls”.
author: Ars Technica

title: Tesla plans to sell Cybercab by year‑end amid safety‑standard probe
content: Tesla announced Wednesday that it will begin selling its gold‑hued Cybercab to customers by the end of the year. The autonomous two‑seater lacks a steering wheel and other traditional controls, and federal regulators are currently investigating whether the vehicle complies with safety standards. The plan was outlined by Lars Moravy, Tesla’s vice president of engineering, during the third‑quarter earnings call.
summary: Tesla announced on Wednesday it will begin selling its gold‑hued, autonomous two‑seat Cybercab, which lacks a steering wheel, to customers by the end of the year. Federal regulators are investigating whether the vehicle meets vehicle safety standards, and Lars Moravy, vice president of engineering at Tesla, discussed the plan during the third‑quarter earnings call.
author: TechCrunch

title: El Salvador launches military operation in Haiti to rescue four kidnapped aviation technicians
content: El Salvador has begun a military operation in Haiti to rescue four aviation technicians who were kidnapped. President Nayib Bukele warned that the men, missing since a Sunday attack on an armoured vehicle, must be freed or a far more powerful operation will follow.
summary: El Salvador has begun a military operation in Haiti to free four aviation technicians who have been missing since a Sunday attack on an armoured vehicle. President Bukele warned that failure to free them would trigger a far more powerful operation.
author: Euronews

title: Macron rejects Trump’s migrant blame for French riots, arrives in Saudi Arabia
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron has rejected claims that migrants were responsible for the violent protests in France on October 17, calling the remarks of “foreign leaders” unacceptable. He condemned the comments as unfounded and unrelated to the demonstrations.  

Macron has now arrived in Saudi Arabia, continuing his Gulf tour.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said he rejects Trump’s claim that migrants caused the French riots. He condemned comments by foreign leaders about the October 17 protests and arrived in Saudi Arabia on his Gulf tour.
author: France 24

title: Kremlin says ready to resume US-Ukraine-Russia talks in mid-November
content: The Kremlin announced on Wednesday that Moscow is ready to resume trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine next month. The statement followed President Vladimir Putin’s meeting with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in Russia. France 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg reports the development.
summary: Moscow is ready to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks next month, the Kremlin said Wednesday after President Vladimir Putin met with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Russia. FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg has more.
author: France 24

title: French President Emmanuel Macron makes surprise solidarity stop in Riyadh
content: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh on Wednesday, adding an unscheduled stop to his Gulf tour. The president’s office said the visit was to demonstrate France’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks on its territory, according to FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Douglas Herbert.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh on Wednesday, adding an unscheduled stop to his Gulf tour. His office said the visit was to demonstrate France's solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.
author: France 24

title: UN says world on track for 2.6°C warming, missing Paris 1.5°C limit
content:
The United Nations Environment Programme has warned that current global commitments to reduce emissions are significantly below the Paris Agreement’s target of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius. The report indicates that the world is currently on track for 2.6 degrees Celsius of warming this century, highlighting a substantial gap between political rhetoric and actual climate action.

This finding sets the stage for political leaders at the upcoming COP31 climate summit, which is scheduled to take place next month in Turkey. The report underscores the urgent challenge facing these leaders as they address the discrepancy between existing pledges and the necessary steps to meet international climate goals.
summary: UN says world on track for 2.6°C warming, missing Paris 1.5°C limit.
author: France 24

title: Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Champions League, Mbappe scores
content: Real Madrid defeated RB Leipzig 4‑1 in a Champions League match on Wednesday, marking their third straight victory in the competition. Goals for Jose Mourinho’s side came from Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler, Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande, while Tidiam Gomis scored for Leipzig. Mbappé has now scored in all three European matches this season, taking his tally to 12 goals.
summary: Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, securing a third consecutive Champions League victory. Kylian Mbappe, Bernardo Silva, Arda Guler and Yan Diomande scored for Madrid, Tidiam Gomis for Leipzig, and Mbappe's goal gave him 12 goals in three European matches this season.
author: France 24

title: Ireland parliament votes 79-71 to end UN approval for overseas peacekeeping
content: Irish lawmakers voted on Wednesday to repeal the rule that requires United Nations approval before Irish military peacekeepers can be sent abroad, passing the legislation by a margin of 79 votes to 71. Opposition members warned the change could jeopardise Ireland’s long‑standing policy of military neutrality, noting that while the country is not a NATO member, it has traditionally taken part in international peace‑keeping missions.
summary: Irish lawmakers voted Wednesday to scrap the UN approval requirement for deploying military peacekeepers overseas, passing the legislation by 79 votes to 71. Opposition members warned the change threatens Ireland’s longstanding military neutrality, though the country is not a NATO member and has traditionally participated in peacekeeping missions.
author: France 24

title: Russian missiles strike Kyiv, wounding six as Moscow signals peace‑talk readiness
content: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and prompting residents to seek shelter, Ukrainian authorities said Thursday. The attack came hours after Moscow signaled readiness to resume US‑mediated peace talks. President Donald Trump said negotiations were closer than ever to ending the war, while the Kremlin voiced doubts about Ukrainian and European proposals.
summary: Russian missiles struck Kyiv overnight, wounding six people and forcing residents into shelters, Ukrainian authorities said. Hours later Moscow signaled readiness to resume US‑mediated peace talks, while President Donald Trump said negotiations were closer than ever, though the Kremlin expressed doubts over Ukrainian and European proposals.
author: France 24

title: Paris police ban protests after violent unrest, Macron accuses Trump of exploiting violence
content: French police imposed a ban on protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as authorities prepared for additional demonstrations after some of the worst street unrest in years. The restrictions followed President Emmanuel Macron’s apparent accusation that U.S. President Donald Trump was exploiting the violence for political gain ahead of the American midterm elections.
summary: French police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as authorities braced for further demonstrations after some of the worst street unrest in years. President Emmanuel Macron appeared to accuse US President Donald Trump of exploiting the violence for political gain ahead of US midterm elections.
author: France 24

title: Waitrose opens first new supermarket in eight years at Cricklewood, north London
content:
Waitrose will open a new supermarket in Cricklewood, north London, on Thursday, marking the grocer’s first new supermarket in eight years. The store is part of a £1 billion investment plan that also includes a second supermarket in Hale Barns, Greater Manchester, scheduled to open next month.

Under the same plan, Waitrose intends to add four smaller outlets next year: a supermarket in Oakham, Rutland, and convenience stores in Bedminster, Bristol; Chalk Farm, London; and Springstead Village, Cambridge.
summary: Waitrose opens first new supermarket in eight years at Cricklewood, north London.
author: Guardian World

title: US diplomats ordered to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
content:
The U.S. State Department has ordered some diplomats and the families of U.S. government employees to leave Saudi Arabia as the kingdom endures a barrage of near‑daily attacks, including an incident on Wednesday evening that killed at least three people at an airport and an oilfield. The drawdown was attributed to attacks on “civilian airports and other critical infrastructure” by the Iranian‑supported Houthis in Yemen. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the safety and security of department personnel and their families remain the highest priority.

Reports also indicate similar withdrawals of U.S. personnel from the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, driven by concerns about a possible return to conflict with Iran following the U.S. midterm elections.
summary: US diplomats ordered to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.
author: Guardian World

title: Canadian publisher Boréal cuts ties with novelist Thélyson Orélien over AI allegations
content:
Canadian publisher Les Éditions du Boréal has ended its relationship with novelist Thélyson Orélien amid allegations that he used artificial intelligence to help write his novel C’était ça ou mourir (“It Was Either That or Die”). Orélien, a top‑selling Haitian‑Canadian writer who was withdrawn from France’s Prix Goncourt list last month, has repeatedly denied using AI on the breakthrough work.

The publisher had earlier, last week, said it was standing by the 38‑year‑old author, but the decision to sever ties follows the confirmed AI involvement.
summary: Les Éditions du Boréal announced it is ending its relationship with Haitian‑Canadian writer Thélyson Orélien after confirming he used artificial intelligence to help write his novel C’était ça ou mourir. Orélien, who was withdrawn from the Prix Goncourt list last month, has repeatedly denied using AI.
author: Guardian World

title: Sam Wood seeks bail in Queensland Supreme Court after domestic violence arrest
content:
Former reality television star and wellness influencer Sam Wood will apply to the Queensland Supreme Court for release from custody. Wood, a 46-year-old from Melbourne, was arrested in Noosa on 4 October facing domestic violence allegations. He stands accused of choking and assaulting his wife.

The court application comes more than two weeks after Wood was initially denied bail.
summary: Sam Wood, a 46-year-old former reality TV star and wellness influencer from Melbourne, was arrested at Noosa on 4 October on domestic violence allegations. He will appear in the Queensland Supreme Court seeking release from custody after being denied bail.
author: Guardian World

title: Perth man charged for threatening staff with nunchucks at Hannah Beazley’s office
content:
A man in Perth has been charged with “being armed in a way that may cause fear” after allegedly threatening staff and brandishing nunchucks at the electoral office of Western Australian local‑government minister Hannah Beazley. The charge follows the incident, which police say involved the suspect wielding the weapon while confronting employees at the office.

The Perth case occurred days after federal independent MP Helen Haines was reported to have been attacked with a 4WD outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, an incident that left her hospitalized with severe injuries.
summary: Perth man charged for threatening staff with nunchucks at Hannah Beazley’s office.
author: Guardian World

title: Victorian antiques store owner fined after 700 frozen and taxidermied animals seized
content:
A 74‑year‑old antiques store owner in Victoria pleaded guilty to 13 charges after a regulator discovered more than 700 native animals that had been illegally taxidermied and frozen on his home and in his shop. The animals, including magpies, galahs, sulphur‑crested cockatoos, foxes and possums, were seized from the property last year.

Following the guilty plea, the man was fined for the offences. The seized specimens were displayed in a white‑walled room, where the frozen animals lay silent on shelves.
summary: A 74‑year‑old Victorian antiques store owner pleaded guilty to 13 charges after regulators uncovered more than 700 illegally taxidermied and frozen native animals at his home and shop. He was subsequently fined for the violations.
author: Guardian World

title: Whale carcass forces closure of Maroubra and Coogee beaches in Sydney
content:
Swimming has been banned at Maroubra and Coogee after a whale carcass washed up between the two beaches in Sydney’s eastern suburbs. Council officials said they will take a “culturally respectful” approach to the remains and have no plans to remove the heavily decomposed body.

The whale was discovered on Thursday morning at Lurline Bay, a rocky cove surrounded by cliffs. The find forced the closure of the two busy swimming and surfing spots while authorities determine how to handle the situation.
summary: Swimming has been banned at Maroubra and Coogee beaches after a heavily decomposed whale carcass washed up at Lurline Bay on Thursday morning. Council officials say they will take a culturally respectful approach to the remains and have no plans to remove the whale.
author: Guardian World

title: Kim Yo-jong says North Korea will restart border propaganda loudspeakers within days
content:
Kim Yo‑jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong‑un, announced that propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border. The statement, issued by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, followed her inspection of border fortifications amid rising tensions between the two countries.

Kim Yo‑jong had previously said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October, indicating a rapid move to resume the broadcasts as bilateral ties worsen.
summary: Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, announced the loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border. The statement was carried by KCNA on Thursday, a day after she said the loudspeakers would operate from some time in October while inspecting border fortifications amid rising tensions.
author: Guardian World

title: Vance urges Republicans to stop whining over Ohio attack ad
content: Vance told Republicans to stop whining about the controversial Ohio attack ad. The ad, produced by Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, features his Democratic rival’s estranged mother, who she has not seen since her stepfather was charged with sexual abuse in her childhood.
summary: Vance told Republicans to stop whining about a controversial Ohio attack ad. The ad by Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy features his Democratic rival's estranged mother, who has not seen her since her stepfather was charged with sexual abuse in her childhood.
author: BBC World

title: Silva sparks Real Madrid's 4-1 demolition of Leipzig in Champions League
content:
Real Madrid secured a third consecutive Champions League victory by defeating RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring from close range near the end of the first half, while Arda Guler extended the lead shortly after the break. Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande also contributed to the goals for José Mourinho’s team.

In other matches, Galatasaray defeated Lille, and Inter Milan edged past Shakhtar with ten men. The results were part of a broader Champions League matchday featuring several decisive outcomes.
summary: Real Madrid secured their third Champions League win by defeating RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday. Bernardo Silva opened the scoring, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande also contributing goals for José Mourinho's side.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck face uncertain future as ESPN contract talks stall
content:
Troy Aikman and Joe Buck have become one of the most lucrative and successful broadcasting teams in American sports, even as television audiences for live sports continue to decline. The pair’s partnership on Monday Night Football has drawn large ratings, but insiders say the duo may not stay together for much longer.

Aikman, who ended his NFL playing career in 2001 because of an aching body, now feels his voice remains in fine working order. Despite that, he has said that ESPN’s bosses may not agree and that the network does not want to renew his contract, leaving his future in the booth uncertain.

Buck, Aikman’s play‑by‑play partner, has signed a new six‑season deal with ESPN worth $108 million. His previous contract covered five years at $15 million per season. The contrast between Buck’s secured deal and Aikman’s reported contract uncertainty highlights the potential split of the once‑united broadcasting power couple.
summary: Joe Buck has agreed to a new six‑season deal with ESPN worth $108 million. Troy Aikman says his voice is still fine, but ESPN reportedly does not want to renew his contract, leaving the duo’s future together in doubt.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Former Australia sprint champion Jake Doran charged with alleged child abuse
content: Police charge 26-year-old with indecent treatment of child under 16 Australian Athletics ban sprinter from any involvement in the sport Australia’s 2022 men’s 100m sprint champion has been arrested in Townsville for alleged indecent treatment of children. Queensland police arrested Jake Doran on 13 October and he has been charged with one count of “indecent treatment of child under 16 (indecent film etc)”. Police investigations covered the period between January 2025 and September 2026. The 26-year-old was bailed to appear at Townsville magistrates court on 5 November.
summary: Former Australia sprint champion Jake Doran charged with alleged child abuse.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carrick's future in doubt after Manchester United's 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como
content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick’s future is in the balance following a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday night. Carrick apologized to fans for the loss, which occurred before Bournemouth’s scheduled visit to Old Trafford on Sunday. His position may be discussed by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner who controls sporting policy.

The defeat prompted criticism from the team’s captain, who hit out at United’s tactics. The captain specifically criticized a “decision from the staff” not to press, highlighting internal dissatisfaction with the tactical approach that led to the humiliating result.
summary: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United manager is under review following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League. Captain Bruno Fernandes criticized the staff's decision not to press, while Carrick apologized to fans for the defeat.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Warnock calls Man Utd's 4-1 Champions League loss to Como 'not good enough'
content: Match of the Day pundits Nedum Onuoha and Stephen Warnock analyse Manchester United's performance after their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como, and discuss midfielder Bruno Fernandes' criticism of team tactics.
summary: Match of the Day pundits Nedum Onuoha and Stephen Warnock analyzed Manchester United's 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. The discussion also covered midfielder Bruno Fernandes' criticism of the team's tactics.
author: BBC Sport

title: Real Madrid beat Leipzig 4-1 for third straight Champions League win
content: Real Madrid extended their perfect Champions League record with a comfortable 4-1 victory over Leipzig, marking their third consecutive win. Bernardo Silva scored his first goal for the club since transferring from Manchester City in the summer.
summary: Real Madrid defeated Leipzig 4-1 to maintain their 100 percent start in the Champions League. Bernardo Silva scored his first goal for Madrid since transferring from Manchester City in the summer.
author: BBC Sport

title: Aston Villa Beat Viking to Maintain Perfect Champions League Start
content: Aston Villa secured their third consecutive Champions League victory by defeating Norwegian side Viking. This dominant performance moved the club up to second place in the league phase standings.
summary: Aston Villa defeated Norwegian side Viking to win their third consecutive Champions League match. This dominant victory moved the team up to second place in the league phase.
author: BBC Sport

title: Rice late goal earns Arsenal draw against Bayern Munich
content: Declan Rice scored a late equalizer to secure a draw for Arsenal against Bayern Munich in the Champions League league phase. The match, described as entertaining, also saw Bukayo Saka limp off with an early injury.
summary: Declan Rice scored a late equalizer to secure a draw for Arsenal against Bayern Munich in the Champions League league phase. Bukayo Saka limped off with an early injury during the entertaining match.
author: BBC Sport

title: Arteta says Saka's quadriceps injury 'does not look good at all'
content: Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the Champions League draw with Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".
summary: Arteta says Saka's quadriceps injury 'does not look good at all'.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man Utd humbled by four-goal Como to pile pressure on Carrick
content: Manchester United suffered a heavy four-goal defeat to Como, a team playing only its third-ever Champions League match. Nico Paz starred for the hosts in the victory, which increased pressure on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick.
summary: Manchester United suffer a heavy defeat to a Como side playing just their third ever game of Champions League football, as Nico Paz stars for the hosts to pile the pressure on Michael Carrick.
author: BBC Sport

title: DNC denies Bankhead claim of job offer to drop Montana Senate race
content: Democrat Alani Bankhead claimed in a recent interview that the Democratic National Committee offered her a job in exchange for dropping her Montana Senate campaign. The DNC has denied this allegation. Bankhead is currently running for the open Senate seat against Independent Seth Bodnar and Republican Kurt Alme.
summary: Democrat Alani Bankhead stated she was offered a DNC job to withdraw from the Montana Senate race, an allegation the DNC denies. She is currently running against Independent Seth Bodnar and Republican Kurt Alme for the open Senate seat.
author: The Hill

title: Fewer Americans say federal government improving their lives: Gallup
content: The Bentley University-Gallup Business in Society survey, released Wednesday, indicates that fewer Americans than last year believe the federal government effectively improves lives. Approximately 43 percent of respondents stated that the government has been effective in making a positive impact on people’s lives.
summary: Fewer Americans than last year think the federal government is effective at making a positive impact on people’s lives, according to a new poll released Wednesday. In the Bentley University-Gallup Business in Society survey, about 43 percent of respondents said the federal government has been effective in making a positive impact on people’s lives.
author: The Hill

title: Rep. Nancy Mace calls Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio ad the most offensive of the cycle
content: Rep. Nancy Mace (R-S. C.) called a controversial political ad run by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy (R) “shameful,” saying she thinks it will hurt Republicans up and down the ballot in Ohio. “This ad is going to go down as the most shameful, disgusting, offensive ad this election season,” Mace told CNN’s Jake Tapper on…
summary: Rep. Nancy Mace calls Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio ad the most offensive of the cycle.
author: The Hill

title: Pennsylvania warns doctors of rising congenital measles risk amid worst outbreak in decades
content: Pennsylvania officials warned doctors this week about an increase in congenital measles as the state continues to battle the worst outbreak in the disease it has seen in decades. The warning follows rising case numbers, prompting heightened vigilance among healthcare providers.
summary: Pennsylvania officials warned doctors this week about an increase in congenital measles. The state is battling the worst measles outbreak it has seen in decades.
author: The Hill

title: Trump to hold rally in Mississippi next Monday
content: The Republican National Committee announced on Wednesday that President Trump is scheduled to hold a rally in Mississippi next Monday. This last-minute midterm event is described as a notable choice given the state’s reliably Republican history, raising concerns that even strong GOP areas may be in play weeks before the election.
summary: President Trump is scheduled to hold a rally in Mississippi next Monday. The Republican National Committee announced the event on Wednesday.
author: The Hill

title: Poll: Voters Trust Democrats More on Issues, Want Congress to Check Trump
content: A new poll indicates record support for Democratic congressional candidates heading into the midterms. The results show that voters believe the party is better equipped to address their primary concerns. Additionally, the data reveals that voters want Congress to serve as a check on President Trump and trust Democrats more on key issues.
summary: A new poll indicates record support for Democratic congressional candidates ahead of the midterms. Voters believe the party is better attuned to handling their top issues and want Congress to act as a check on Trump.
author: NPR Politics

title: Ramaswamy ad features mother of Democrat Amy Acton
content: A campaign ad for Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy features the mother of Democrat Amy Acton. Acton states that she has been estranged from her mother since childhood, alleging that she was abused by her stepfather.
summary: A campaign ad for Republican Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy includes the mother of Democrat Amy Acton. Acton states they have been estranged since she was abused as a child by her stepfather.
author: NPR Politics

title: Iran war gives California Democrats rare chance to counter high gas prices
content: California gas prices remain the highest in the nation, a factor that has historically plagued Democratic candidates. However, the ongoing war in Iran has provided these Democrats with a rare opportunity to shift the political narrative on the issue.
summary: California gas prices remain the highest in the nation. The war in Iran provides California Democrats a rare opportunity to turn the tables on the issue.
author: NPR Politics

title: Infrared light creates green letters less prone to blur
content: ICTER scientists have investigated how visible images generated by near-infrared light behave when they are no longer perfectly focused. While infrared light is inherently invisible, specific pulses can produce a visible image within the eye that exhibits counterintuitive properties.
summary: ICTER scientists investigated how visible images generated by near-infrared light behave when imperfectly focused. The resulting green letters are less prone to blur under these conditions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: POSTECH AI identifies tumor aging patterns to predict immunotherapy response
content: A research team at POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology) has developed an artificial intelligence technology to predict which patients are likely to benefit from immunotherapy. This AI identifies tumor aging patterns to forecast treatment responses across multiple cancer types, addressing the variability where some patients respond well to the same drug while others show little to no response.
summary: A research team at POSTECH developed an AI technology to predict which patients are likely to benefit from immunotherapy. The system analyzes tumor aging patterns to address the variability in patient responses to the same drug.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Single tooth yields six identity clues for forensic identification
content:
Researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo have demonstrated that a single tooth can yield six distinct types of information to aid in identifying deceased individuals. By applying multiple forensic methods to various tissues within one tooth, the study shows that valuable clues about a person’s identity can be extracted even when remains are severely decomposed or reduced to bones.

This integrated approach offers complementary evidence for identifying unknown human remains, particularly in cases where conventional identification methods are difficult to apply. The findings highlight the potential of dental forensics to provide critical insights from minimal biological material.
summary: Researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo found that a single tooth can provide six types of information about a deceased person. This integrated forensic approach helps identify unknown remains when conventional methods are difficult to apply.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UGA Review: Screen Time Effects on Children Depend on More Than Duration
content: A new publication from the University of Georgia suggests that the effects of screen time on young children may depend on factors beyond just the duration of device use. The study, which challenges the notion that all screen time is harmful, has been published in the Journal of Evidence-Based Social Work.
summary: A new publication from the University of Georgia suggests that the effects of screen time on young children depend on factors beyond just the time spent on devices. The study was published in the Journal of Evidence-Based Social Work.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts urge green transition funds to finance universal health coverage
content: Experts writing in The BMJ's climate issue suggest that the green energy transition offers a key chance to fund universal health coverage in low- and middle-income countries.
summary: Experts in The BMJ's climate issue say the green energy transition can finance universal health coverage in low- and middle-income countries. They view it as a crucial opportunity.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts warn wars degrade water systems, harming health and recovery
content: Experts warn in The BMJ’s climate issue that while water scarcity rarely initiates wars, conflicts increasingly damage essential water systems. These systems are critical for health and recovery, and their degradation creates a cycle that reinforces ongoing fragility and violence.
summary: Experts say wars are increasingly degrading vital water systems that health and recovery depend on. They warn this creates a reinforcing cycle of fragility and violence, as reported in The BMJ's climate issue.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Eye tracking and AI could personalize virtual reality pain therapy
content: World-first research from the University of East Anglia suggests that combining artificial intelligence with eye tracking in virtual reality could personalize treatment for individuals with chronic pain. The study indicates this technology may help adapt therapy to individual needs for millions living with the condition.
summary: Research from the University of East Anglia suggests that combining artificial intelligence with eye tracking in virtual reality could help personalize treatment. This approach aims to address the needs of millions of people living with chronic pain.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Expert calls for systemic changes to agri-food supply chain to combat global food shortages
content: An expert writing in The BMJ’s climate issue argues that systemic changes across the entire agri‑food supply chain are required to address the global impact of conflict and climate change on food shortages.
summary: Systemic changes across the entire agri-food supply chain are needed to address the global impact of conflict and climate change on food shortages. An expert wrote this in The BMJ's climate issue.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers review Candida auris and potential for new fungal threats
content: Researchers at the Biocentre of the University of Würzburg, Carla Schuh and Chaitanya Gokhale, have published a review article in the journal mSphere addressing the rapid emergence of the yeast Candida auris as a dangerous global pathogen. In their study, the authors analyzed approximately 180 studies conducted by other researchers to summarize the current state of scientific knowledge on the issue.
summary: Carla Schuh and Chaitanya Gokhale from the University of Würzburg published a review in mSphere analyzing why Candida auris became a dangerous pathogen. The study summarizes the current state of knowledge by analyzing around 180 studies by other researchers.
author: Phys.org

title: U.K. exam board science specifications reveal gender gap that may influence girls' STEM choices
content: New research from the University of Cambridge indicates that the absence of women scientists in U.K. exam board science specifications may contribute to the disproportionate number of girls dropping STEM subjects at 16. The study suggests this lack of representation could also be a factor in the broader gender gap within STEM careers.
summary: U.K. exam board science specifications reveal gender gap that may influence girls' STEM choices.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers develop optogenetic tools to inhibit neuron and heart cell activity
content: Researchers from Ruhr University Bochum, collaborating with colleagues in Göttingen, Berlin, Paris, and Essen, have developed new optogenetic tools that selectively inhibit cellular activity using light. These tools are designed to help investigate diseases where the balance between excitation and inhibition is disrupted, including cardiac arrhythmias.
summary: Researchers from Ruhr University Bochum and partners developed new optogenetic tools that selectively inhibit cellular activity using light. These tools may aid in investigating diseases involving disrupted excitation-inhibition balances, such as cardiac arrhythmias.
author: Phys.org

title: Kindergarten redshirting and retention shifted sharply during the pandemic
content: By the time a child reaches the age of 4 or 5, most parents and caregivers have heard about "kindergarten readiness." But what if a 5-year-old still struggles to count to 10, sing the alphabet song or play cooperatively with other children?
summary: The article examines kindergarten readiness challenges, such as counting and social play, for children aged 4 or 5. It notes that practices like redshirting and retention changed significantly during the pandemic.
author: Phys.org

title: Venomous primate lost for decades found in Indonesian gardens and on roads
content: A venomous primate, last documented in scientific literature in the 1930s, has been discovered across the Indonesian island of Bangka. These big-eyed animals are frequently found in backyards, along roadsides, and on power lines. Local residents who encounter them have been contacting the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center for assistance.
summary: A venomous primate not documented in scientific literature since the 1930s has been observed on the Indonesian island of Bangka. Local residents frequently encounter the animal in backyards and along roadsides, prompting calls to the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center.

title: AI monitors bee activity via buzzes to avoid lethal traps
content:
Pollinator populations, including bumblebees, have declined significantly over recent decades due to chemical pesticides, habitat loss, and climate change. Accurately measuring these populations and evaluating conservation efforts remains difficult because traditional methods often rely on lethal traps that kill tens of thousands of bees to obtain precise counts.

To address this challenge, researchers are developing an AI system that listens to bee buzzes to monitor activity. This non-lethal approach aims to provide population data without the need for traps that result in significant bee mortality.
summary: AI technology analyzes bee buzzes to monitor pollinator activity without using lethal traps. This method avoids killing bees to obtain population counts amid declining pollinator populations.
author: Phys.org

title: Bose acquires Skullcandy, will keep brand separate in premium audio unit
content:
Bose has announced the acquisition of Skullcandy, a move intended to help the company reach a wider audience. Although the two firms compete in the consumer audio sector, Skullcandy recently partnered with Bose to integrate specific technologies, including head-tracking spatial audio and active noise cancellation, into products such as the Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and Method 360 ANC earbuds.

The deal’s specific financial details were not disclosed. According to a news release, Bose intends to maintain Skullcandy as a distinct brand within its premium consumer audio business. Skullcandy will continue to be based in Park City, Utah.
summary: Bose announced it has acquired Skullcandy and will keep Skullcandy as a separate brand within its premium consumer audio business. Skullcandy will remain based in Park City, Utah and has already added Bose head‑tracking spatial audio and active noise cancellation to products such as the Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and Method 360 ANC earbuds.

title: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
content:
Tesla reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $1.7 billion on revenue of $28.0 billion, marking a flat quarter compared to the previous year. While the company’s earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations of $27.9 billion, they fell short of Tesla’s internal forecast of $28.3 billion. Net income declined by 4 percent relative to the third quarter of 2025, when the automaker recorded $1.4 billion in profit on $28.1 billion in revenue.

The financial results were released following a recent Roadster demo. According to data compiled by LSEG, the reported figures indicate that the company’s top line has stalled, despite the hype surrounding its new vehicle demonstration.
summary: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues.
author: The Verge

title: Critical PHP bugs force major sites and government agencies offline
content:
Two AI-discovered critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language have caused significant disruptions across the internet, affecting major platforms including 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia, and various blogs. Because PHP underpins much of the web, including sites built on WordPress, the impact extends beyond these specific examples. In response to the threat, several Dutch and Finnish government agencies preemptively took their websites offline.

Cybersecurity authorities have advised organizations to take systems offline if immediate updates are not feasible. This recommendation was issued by both the NSA Cybersecurity account on X and the UK’s National Cyber Security Center. The widespread nature of the issue has also impacted other services, with the source noting effects on Pokémon Home and Pokémon C.
summary: Critical vulnerabilities discovered in the PHP programming language have caused major outages for sites including 4chan, DeviantArt, and Wikipedia. Cybersecurity agencies in the UK and US recommended taking systems offline if an immediate update is not feasible.
author: The Verge

title: New York's first microdrama film festival Alza debuts October 16-18
content:
Alza, New York City’s first microdrama film festival, took place from October 16 to 18, serving as a showcase for stories created for vertical screens. The event was founded by Pete Torres, the former chief operating officer of the Tribeca Festival, and was billed as a platform to highlight the creativity, innovation, and growing cultural impact of this new format.

The festival featured a selection of microdrama and film premieres alongside industry-focused panels with executives. Attendees included actors Taye Diggs, Autumn Federici, Gary Entin, Troy Brookins, Edmund Entin, and Eric Guilmette, who were present for the world premiere of Reunion Island, a production by Microhouse Films and Lifetime. While many filmmakers and creators expressed confidence that their projects would resonate with audiences, it remains to be seen if viewers are eager to watch vertical content on traditional horizontal TV screens.
summary: Alza, founded by former Tribeca Festival chief operating officer Pete Torres, took place in New York City from October 16th through 18th as the city's first microdrama film festival. The event showcased premieres and industry panels focused on stories made for the vertical screen.

title: Meta to issue new non-voting shares to fund AI initiatives
content:
Meta announced the creation of a new class of non-voting shares to finance its artificial intelligence initiatives, potential acquisitions, and employee compensation. The company revealed this plan in its third-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday, noting that trading for the new stock is expected to begin in 2027. Meta stated that the substantial investment is necessary to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue strategic initiatives during the industry’s AI transformation.

Susan Li, Meta’s chief financial officer, explained during an earnings call that the new shares will expand the company’s funding tools.
summary: Meta announced it will create a new class of non-voting shares to fund AI initiatives, potential acquisitions, and employee compensation. Trading for the new stock is scheduled to begin in 2027.

title: Stern Pinball tours showcase 90% market share at Pinball Expo 2026
content:
The Pinball Expo 2026 drew pinball enthusiasts to a convention center in Chicagoland this October, marking a return of the medium to the spotlight after a period of decline. The event began with a large crowd outside the headquarters of Stern Pinball in Elk Grove, Illinois, where visitors waited for a tour of the company’s factory and offices.

The author was welcomed by Gary Stern, who provided a brief history of the company’s 40‑year legacy. After a stop at Gary’s podium, the group was led to the factory floor where George Gomez, a Stern employee and renowned game designer, explained the tour rules and answered questions. Gomez noted that Stern “controls 90 percent of the current pinball market, and everybody else splits the rest.”

The tour took place before the convention’s main sessions in nearby Schaumburg, Illinois, giving attendees a firsthand look at the production of new “silver‑ball” games and the enduring appeal of classic machines.
summary: At the Pinball Expo 2026 in the Chicago area, Stern Pinball hosted tours of its headquarters and factory in Elk Grove, Illinois. During the tour, Gary Stern highlighted the company's 40‑year history and George Gomez said Stern controls about 90 percent of the current pinball market.

title: Review: Carrie is a triumphant remix with one major flaw
content:
Mike Flanagan’s eight-episode Prime Video miniseries, Carrie, has been released to coincide with the 50th anniversary of Brian De Palma’s 1976 film adaptation. The project reimagines the story of Carrie White, a telekinetic character first introduced in Stephen King’s 1974 novel and popularized by De Palma’s widely acclaimed movie. The new series faces significant expectations given the legacy of the original film, which is considered one of the best horror films and King adaptations of all time.

The review notes that while some viewers initially questioned the necessity of a new adaptation, Flanagan, a noted fan of horror and King’s work, delivers a richly textured version of the story. The miniseries is described as a "triumphant remix" that balances themes of kindness and lost innocence with the expected elements of bloody, vengeful rage. However, the review highlights that this success comes with one major flaw, though the specific nature of this exception is not detailed in the provided text. The article includes spoilers for the novel and the 1976 film, with a warning that major reveals for the new series occur after the second gallery.
summary: Carrie White, the telekinetic prom queen from hell, is one of the most beloved horror icons in popular culture. First introduced in Stephen King's 1974 novel, Carrie, the character was immortalized in director Brian De Palma's 1976 adaptation, widely regarded as one of the best horror films of all time.

title: Xbox introduces Cloud Playtime purchases at 24 to 40 cents per hour
content:
Microsoft has rolled out a new service to Xbox Insiders that allows non-subscribers to purchase cloud playtime hours to stream games they already own. This feature was previously announced in September when the company limited game-streaming access for Game Pass subscribers, stating that users could soon buy playtime through the Xbox Store. The new a la carte option is now available on supported devices for those who do not have an active subscription.

The introductory launch pricing for these Cloud Playtime purchases is structured in three tiers: 10 hours for $4, 25 hours for $8, and 50 hours for $12. These prices equate to approximately $0.40, $0.32, and $0.24 per hour, respectively. Microsoft notes that purchased playtime remains available until it is used, meaning the hours do not expire before they are fully consumed. This pricing model applies specifically to players who have already purchased the eligible games they wish to stream.
summary: Microsoft has rolled out a la carte Cloud Playtime purchases to Xbox Insiders, allowing users to stream eligible games they already own. The introductory pricing ranges from $4 for 10 hours to $12 for 50 hours, with purchased playtime remaining available until used.

content: Scientists studying captive orangutans observed that the apes were more likely to select treats when the food was paired with the sound of their peers laughing. title: Clayface review: Gory but middling DC film starring Liverpool as Gotham
content: Liverpool makes for an unconvincing Gotham City in this effectively gross but otherwise middling attempt to milk money from a lesser-known Batman villain A sense of desperation is understandably in the air over at DC, the company, like Marvel, slowly realising that the mass superhero fever has finally broken. There’s still interest there, of course (this summer’s Spider-Man is now the biggest film of all time in the US after all), but it’s no longer good enough to leave a high-speed conveyor belt unmanned, purpose and quality control be damned. 2019 saw a staggering 10 superhero films released in cinemas, and the inevitable exhaustion that followed, also fueled by Covid, led to a gradual winding down, monster hits turning into minor ones and sure bets often becoming expensive flops. As Peter Parker winged his way to box office records this summer, DC’s Supergirl bombed so hard that experts believe it might have cost Warners upwards of $200m in losses. It was just the latest disappointment for the brand after Black Adam, Joker: Folie à Deux, Blue Beetle and The Flash all underperformed while even last year’s much-heralded Superman reboot only grossed a solid $618m, a far cry from the $1bn heyday of the genre (things got so bad that even a fully filmed Batgirl adventure was deleted for the tax break ). Notably, the last DC film to swoop past that magic figure was Joker in 2019, a darker, lower-budget attempt to spotlight a villain rather than a hero, a big swing with relatively low stakes. Todd Phillips’s film might be best known by some for being brave enough to ask the question, “What if Taxi Driver sucked?” but for all of its many issues, it brought buzz and prestige and, shockingly, Oscars, to an easily ridiculed universe. It was also, crucially, something rare in that world: a close-to-good idea.
summary: The review describes the film as effectively gross but otherwise middling, criticizing Liverpool as an unconvincing Gotham City. It notes that the movie is a desperate attempt to milk money from a lesser-known Batman villain amidst a broader decline in DC box office performance.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool after Villarreal win

title: Great Britain finishes fourth in men's team at 2026 Artistic World Championships
content: Great Britain finished fourth in the men’s team final at the 2026 Artistic World Championships, narrowly missing a podium finish. The British squad had led the competition after four rotations, but costly slips on the final apparatuses cost them a medal. Japan went on to claim the gold medal. Britain will have another opportunity to qualify for the LA28 Olympics at the World Championships in Chengdu next year.
summary: Great Britain finished fourth in the men's team final at the 2026 Artistic World Championships after leading the competition for four rotations but slipping on the final apparatuses. Japan claimed gold and Britain will have another chance to qualify for the LA28 Olympics at next year’s World Championships in Chengdu.
author: BBC Sport

title: Paz, Fabregas and Como teach Man Utd a lesson
content: Serie A club Como have progressed from Serie D to the Champions League, marking a significant rise in European football. In their latest encounter, the Italian side delivered a decisive performance that served as a lesson for Manchester United in the competition.

title: Gas, groceries, electricity: Where prices stand as midterms approach
content: September’s inflation increase brought higher prices to Americans ahead of the midterm elections. Democrats are seeking to regain control of Congress from the GOP by emphasizing affordability issues. The consumer price index reported an annual inflation rate of 3.7 percent for last month, with the source noting a monthly rise in the cost of energy, gas, and electricity.

The video, which debuted online, features the mother of Ramaswamy’s opponent, Amy. Husted made these remarks in a statement to the Associated Press on Wednesday.

content: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak announced that Russia will dispatch its first diesel shipment to the United States on Thursday. The vessel is scheduled to transport 40,000 metric tons of fuel, according to a Reuters report citing the RIA news agency. Novak also indicated that additional shipments are expected to follow the initial delivery.
summary: Russia is going to send its first tanker with diesel to the U. S.
author: The Hill

title: Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
content: Top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees stated they are operating under the presumption that President Trump will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield drilling, climate campaigners condemn
content:
Climate campaigners have condemned the UK government’s decision to approve drilling at the Jackdaw gasfield. Critics argue this move jeopardizes climate targets and fails to address energy bills or the cost of living crisis.

Meanwhile, the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is reportedly leaning towards rejecting approval for the much larger Rosebank oilfield. This potential decision could represent a significant victory for green activists. Michael Safi discusses these developments with environment correspondent Matthew Taylor in a YouTube video.
summary: Climate campaigners have condemned the UK government’s decision to allow the drilling of the Jackdaw gasfield. Critics argue the move will put climate targets at risk, while failing to reduce energy bills and the cost of living crisis.
