title: Newcastle, Great Ormond Street researchers find new ALL relapse predictors
content: Researchers from Newcastle University and Great Ormond Street Hospital have identified new predictors of relapse in children and young people with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). This discovery was made during a U.K.-wide study involving patients treated with the immunotherapy drug blinatumomab.
summary: Researchers from Newcastle University and Great Ormond Street Hospital have identified new predictors of relapse in children and young people with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treated with the immunotherapy drug blinatumomab, as part of a U. K.-wide study.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Anticoagulants May Lower Stroke Risk in AFib Patients With Prior Brain Bleeds
content: A new study published in Neurology reports that anticoagulant use is associated with a lower risk of ischemic stroke and death for individuals with atrial fibrillation and a history of intracranial hemorrhage. The research further indicates that taking newer anticoagulants did not increase the risk of additional brain bleeds in these patients.
summary: A study published in Neurology found that anticoagulant use is associated with a lower risk of ischemic stroke and death in patients with atrial fibrillation and intracranial hemorrhage. The research also indicated that taking newer anticoagulants did not increase the risk of additional brain bleeds.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Restoring heart rhythm after stroke and AFib linked to lower repeat stroke risk
content: A new study published in Neurology indicates that restoring normal heart rhythm within eight weeks of an ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of subsequent strokes. This finding applies to patients hospitalized with both ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation.
summary: A study published in Neurology found that restoring normal heart rhythm within eight weeks of an ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of another stroke. This benefit applies to patients hospitalized with both ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: AAO Study Finds No AMD Risk With GLP-1 Receptor Agonists After Adjustments
content: A study presented at the American Academy of Ophthalmology annual meeting in New Orleans explored the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use and age-related macular degeneration. While crude odds ratios indicated an increased risk, this finding reversed after adjusting for cardiometabolic confounding variables.
summary: A study presented at the American Academy of Ophthalmology found that crude odds ratios initially suggested an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration with GLP-1 receptor agonist use. This finding was reversed after adjusting for cardiometabolic confounding variables.
author: Medical Xpress

title: University of Pittsburgh team builds uncertainty-aware AI for breast cancer scans
content:
AI offers the ability to improve human experts’ ability to diagnose and treat diseases like breast cancer, but well‑publicized errors across the broader AI field raise concerns.

A team from the University of Pittsburgh used PSC’s flagship Bridges‑2 supercomputer to design a deep neural network that takes uncertainty into account when diagnosing breast scan images.
summary: AI can help improve diagnosis and treatment of diseases such as breast cancer, though errors in the broader AI field raise concerns. Researchers at the University of Pittsburgh used the PSC Bridges-2 supercomputer to create a deep neural network that incorporates uncertainty when diagnosing breast scan images.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Three-week radiation course a safe option for breast cancer patients undergoing reconstruction, trial shows
content: A national clinical trial led by the Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology, in conjunction with NRG Oncology and the Canadian Cancer Trials Group, indicates that a three-week radiation schedule following a mastectomy is as safe and effective as the standard five-week treatment for women undergoing breast reconstruction. The findings from the RT CHARM trial (Alliance A221505) have been published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology.
summary: Three-week radiation course a safe option for breast cancer patients undergoing reconstruction, trial shows.
author: Medical Xpress

title: How humans domesticated the bacterium behind Botox treatments
content:
Clostridium botulinum bacteria produce the potent neurotoxin botulinum toxin, which causes botulism by attacking the nervous system and paralyzing muscles. Without immediate treatment, the illness can be fatal. Despite this danger, humans have successfully domesticated the bacterium to serve various purposes.

Over a period of more than 90 years, biologists have transformed this wild microbe into an efficient production facility. The bacterium is now used to manufacture medical, military, and cosmetic products, including Botox.
summary: Clostridium botulinum bacteria produce a potent neurotoxin called botulinum toxin, which causes the serious illness botulism. The toxin attacks the nervous system, leaving the body unable to control its muscles and making every breath a struggle.
author: Phys.org

title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
content: New drug active ingredients treating infections, cancer, or other serious diseases are frequently derived from microorganisms, plants, or other living organisms. However, producing or improving these substances in a targeted manner using microorganisms is often challenging due to the extreme complexity of the underlying biological processes.
summary: New active ingredients for drugs to treat infections, cancer or other serious diseases are often based on substances originally discovered in microorganisms, plants or other living organisms. Producing or improving such active ingredients in a targeted manner using microorganisms is often challenging because the underlying biological processes are extremely complex.
author: Phys.org

title: AI-assisted device transmits scents like orange and beer over the internet
content: The familiar scent of orange can now be transmitted through the internet Counter/Getty Images Imagine if, in addition to sharing photos of those muffins you just baked, you could share their delicious aroma, too. That’s the promise of an AI-assisted device that can transmit smells over the internet. So far, it works on only a small number of scents, including orange, beer and cake, but its creators hope the system will ultimately recreate more smells. The scent of a pine forest or the aroma of coffee, for example, could then add a new dimension to virtual worlds and long-distance communication. Although it is now routine to communicate sight, sound and even touch sensations electronically, smell is “still a very undeveloped sense”, says Chunyu Yang at the Ohio State University. That’s partly because odours involve complex chemistry. Whereas vision, for example, can be broken down into combinations of red, green and blue pixels, says Yang, there’s no simple building block underlying smell. Any attempt to convert aromas into electronic signals has to recognise combinations of very different molecules. Smell-seeking drone uses moth antenna to follow a scent To solve the problem, Yang and her colleagues built an electronic nose, or “e-nose”, as well as a smell generator, then used machine learning to connect the two. The e-nose consists of arrays of sensors made of metal oxide. When different gaseous components of smells, such as ethanol (from alcoholic drinks) or limonene (found in citrus fruits), bind to the sensors’ surface, this changes their resistance, creating different electrical signals. Advertisement The researchers then trained an AI algorithm to recognise the distinctive signals created by smells from five different foods or beverages: orange, cake, coffee, beer and red wine. Teaching the AI to correctly recognise the smells was “the most challenging part” of the entire study, says Yang, because to generate enough data to train the system, she had to expose the sensors to the various smells hundreds of times. This information was then sent over the internet to a smell generation device that the researchers are calling “Scentronic”. This part of the system involves miniature containers holding liquids laced with each of the five smells. Above each container is an atomiser that vibrates in response to electric signals, forcing the liquid in the container through a cotton filter and releasing fine droplets into the air, creating the appropriate smell, or combination of smells. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Editor’s Highlights Sign up to newsletter Yang built several different designs including stringing the atomisers onto a necklace and a wristband, and mounting them on a handheld device. When she tested the handheld device on 14 volunteers, they correctly identified the smells being transmitted to them 73 per cent of the time, on average. She also built a prototype that reproduces taste, involving a cup of water with electromagnetic pumps containing flavoured liquid fixed around its edge. “When it receives information from the internet, the corresponding liquid will be dropped into the cup.” Alternative methods to generate smells remotely have been suggested, including heating wax to release particular scents, and even stimulating neurons directly to create the experience of smell. But Yang argues her method is both fast and practical. She now hopes to expand the repertoire of the system, to create more complex aromas. Why honing your sense of smell could keep you sharp as you age A declining ability to detect scents is linked to conditions including Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s. But restoring our most neglected sense might not only reduce cognitive decline – studies also show it could even reverse it She suggests the entertainment industry could be first to develop the technology, to create more immersive virtual worlds. But there could also be health applications. For instance, the smell of food transforms the eating experience, so the technology could be adapted to make soldiers’ or astronauts’ rations more palatable. The Scentronic system could also enable doctors to assess distortions in patients’ sense of smell, for example, in post-viral illness or neurodegenerative disease. The Scentronic system is “a great idea” and a step in the right direction, says Marianna Obrist at University College London, although she points out that recognising a smell and then releasing a matching one from a limited library is very different from the ease with which we can transmit sound and vision. “There’s still a long way to go before we can truly record and replay smell experiences.” Journal Reference: Science Advances DOI: 10.1126/sciadv. Aee9266
summary: Researchers at Ohio State University developed a system that uses an electronic nose and machine learning to transmit specific smells over the internet to a device called Scentronic. The system currently works with five scents, including orange and coffee, and was correctly identified by volunteers 73 percent of the time in tests.
author: New Scientist

title: Study Links 10 Healthy Diets to Slower Biological Aging
content: A study by the DZNE reveals that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging, indicating multiple valid approaches to a nutritious diet. The researchers analyzed ten distinct dietary patterns, including the Mediterranean, Nordic, and plant-based diets, alongside the DASH diet, which is specifically designed to help lower blood pressure. These findings have been published in the journal Nature Communications.
summary: A DZNE study published in Nature Communications found that ten healthy dietary patterns, including Mediterranean and DASH diets, are associated with slower biological aging. The research indicates that there is more than one way to eat healthily to achieve this effect.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find first eyeless freshwater snail in Chinese high‑altitude cave
content: Scientists have discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail deep inside a high-altitude Chinese cave. This species, which has evolved to live entirely in darkness, marks the first recorded discovery of its kind in China. Named after a faceless mythical creature, the rare snail may already be in danger, as researchers found only three living adults.
summary: Scientists discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail deep inside a high‑altitude Chinese cave, the first record of such a species in China. The snail, named after a faceless mythical creature, is rare and may already be endangered, with only three living adults found.
author: Science Daily

title: Adults outscore preschoolers on creativity but feel more anxious, study finds
content:
A new study comparing preschoolers with adults in their 20s challenges the widespread assumption that children are inherently more creative. The research found that adults actually outperform preschoolers on creative tasks. However, the adults reported feeling significantly less confident and more anxious while completing these activities.

The researchers conclude that fear of failure and anxiety are primary factors hampering adult performance. This finding suggests that while adults possess greater creative capability, their hesitation and shyness in creative scenarios stem from these psychological barriers rather than a lack of ability.
summary: The study compared preschoolers with adults, mostly in their 20s, on creative tasks. Adults outperformed the children but reported higher fear of failure and anxiety, which reduced their confidence.
author: Guardian Science

title: Ex-Eventbrite engineer reveals 20-year secret of being a convicted felon
content:
A former engineer, identified as the third engineer at Eventbrite and a founding engineer at Reforge, revealed on Hacker News that he has been a convicted felon for twenty years. The individual, who has also worked at Instacart and founded multiple startups, stated that he never disclosed his criminal record to employers or landlords. He described facing significant barriers, including the inability to rent apartments in San Francisco or secure employment immediately after his release from prison.

The post highlights the financial and personal challenges he faced, noting that owing $17,000 in restitution while unemployed created a desperate situation that risked re-incarceration. Despite these obstacles, the author transitioned from homelessness at age 19 to earning seven figures within a decade, eventually retiring at age 38.

The individual is currently writing an autobiography centered on the theme of hope. He aims to share the experience of sleeping in a car while maintaining the belief that he would one day travel the world, a goal he eventually achieved. The post invites readers to express interest in the book, with a link provided for further discussion.
summary: A former engineer at Eventbrite and Reforge disclosed that he hid his status as a convicted felon for two decades while building multiple startups. He is now writing an autobiography about his journey from homelessness to retiring at age 38 with a theme of hope.
author: Hacker News

title: PHP 8.2.35 Release Discussed on Hacker News
content: PHP released a security update today, accompanied by discussions on enhancing the platform's security measures. The release is linked to ongoing community threads regarding PHP 8.2.35 on Y Combinator News.
summary: PHP 8.2.35 Release Discussed on Hacker News.
author: Hacker News

title: Star Wars Zero Company physical editions 20% off at Amazon
content:
Star Wars Zero Company, a turn-based strategy game set in the Star Wars universe, is currently available at a 20 percent discount on Amazon. The physical edition for PlayStation 5 is priced at $47.99, while the Xbox Series S/X version costs $49.99, down from the standard retail price of $59.99. The game features a character creator that offers numerous unlockable outfits, accessories, and classic alien races from the films and cartoons.

The title includes branching story missions with lasting consequences and higher difficulty modes that impose stricter penalties for errors. Players can lead a crew of heroes in battles against Droidekas and outlaws, with the narrative and characters designed to provide an immersive experience for fans of the Star Wars world.
summary: Star Wars Zero Company physical editions 20% off at Amazon.
author: The Verge

title: Xbox mandates a four-day return to office
content:
Microsoft has increased its return-to-office mandate for most Xbox employees from three to four days per week. According to an internal memo reviewed by The Verge, the change is intended to create more opportunities for collaboration following feedback from staff. Jacinda Chislum Pearson, Xbox chief people officer, stated that the new policy reflects a need for people to work together.

Effective February 1, 2027, Xbox employees in the Puget Sound region who live within 50 commuting miles of Studio D must work from the office at least four days a week. Pearson noted that thousands of Xbox employees are within this commuting distance.
summary: Xbox mandates a four-day return to office.
author: The Verge

title: Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update adds console mods and Edgerunners content
content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is receiving a major 2.5 update that introduces cross-platform mod support for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and Xbox consoles. The patch also delivers content inspired by the new season of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime on Netflix. Among the specific additions tied to the show are a new side quest, a gear set based on the character Weak Kingsley, and a new radio station featuring Edgerunners music.

The update includes additional gameplay features accessible to all players, such as a Double Trouble perk option that enables dual-wielding of pistols and revolvers. It also adds a Richard Night-guided tour of the city side quest, though the provided text is cut off before detailing further elements of the release.
summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is releasing a 2.5 update that brings cross-platform mod support to PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox consoles. The patch also includes Edgerunners-inspired content such as a new side quest, a gear set based on Weak Kingsley, and a dedicated radio station.
author: The Verge

title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal
content:
A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties for more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices law. This ruling, linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, represents the largest legal loss for the company this year, occurring alongside other recent settlements and adverse rulings.

The decision follows a September jury verdict in which jurors found that Meta misled consumers regarding its data protection measures and its efforts to prevent misinformation and hate speech on its platforms. The legal action originated from a complaint filed in 2021, which was prompted by earlier revelations that UK political consultancy Cambridge Analytica harvested data from millions of users.
summary: Mark Zuckerberg. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images The Cambridge Analytica scandal has come back to haunt Meta after a New Mexico judge ordered it to pay $25 billion in penalties for more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices law.
author: The Verge

title: Walmart to let customers connect AI agents for shopping on its site
content:
Walmart announced that it will soon let customers use AI agents to shop on its website. Beginning next month, shoppers can connect their own AI agent to the site, and the retailer has built in controls that allow users to approve and review purchases and set spending limits.  

The company has also issued a set of terms for the agents. Agents must not take actions beyond what the shopper intends, cannot change a customer’s payment method, and can only … (the final restriction was not fully disclosed). Walmart’s move contrasts with Amazon, which has blocked Perplexity’s shopping agent and Meta’s Muse AI assistant.
summary: Walmart will allow shoppers to connect their own AI agents to its website next month, with tools to approve purchases and set spending limits. The retailer’s rules require agents to act only as the shopper intends, forbid changing payment methods, and contrast with Amazon’s blocking of Perplexity’s shopping agent and Meta’s Muse AI assistant.
author: The Verge

title: Airbnb bans hosts from requiring guests to do dishes or laundry
content:
Airbnb has updated its house rules policy to prohibit hosts from requiring guests to perform time-consuming chores. Effective for reservations booked on or after November 20th, the new guidelines state that hosts cannot ask guests to "complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner." This policy aims to reduce the hassle of checking out by removing demanding obligations from guest responsibilities.

Specifically, the ban covers dishwashing and laundry duties. Guests should not be asked to wash and put away dishes, though hosts may still request that used dishes be placed in the sink. Similarly, hosts are prohibited from asking guests to remove sheets from beds or start loads of laundry.
summary: Airbnb's updated house rules policy prohibits hosts from asking guests to complete tasks that require significant effort or time. This ban, which applies to reservations booked on or after November 20th, includes chores like washing dishes and doing laundry.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX to attempt Starship catch on next flight, with eye on rapid cadence increase
content:
During a Tuesday afternoon earnings call, SpaceX officials outlined plans to deploy up to 10 gigawatts of artificial intelligence compute capacity on the ground by 2027. Company leaders emphasized that SpaceX is currently functioning largely as a data company focused on providing extensive compute resources for AI, shifting away from previous aspirational discussions regarding human settlement of Mars.

Despite the focus on terrestrial AI infrastructure, the company’s long-term strategy for providing data services from space remains dependent on the Starship rocket. This includes supporting the Starlink Internet constellation and a future “Starmind” data center constellation. During the same earnings call, SpaceX founder Elon Musk and president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell disclosed new performance targets for the Starship vehicle. These targets are intended to support the next flight attempt, which includes a planned catch maneuver, while aiming for a rapid increase in launch cadence.
summary: In its current iteration, SpaceX is largely a data company seeking to provide enormous amounts of compute for artificial intelligence. During an earnings call on Tuesday afternoon, company officials spent much of their time discussing ambitious plans to roll out up to 10 GW of compute in 2027—on the ground.
author: Ars Technica

title: Research finds Samsung, Vizio, Roku TVs send data after tracking opt-out
content:
Research published on Monday indicates that smart TVs from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue transmitting data to automatic content recognition (ACR) endpoints even after users disable tracking features in their device settings. The study, conducted by researchers at Northeastern University, suggests these practices may constitute privacy violations by major television brands. ACR technology captures video screenshots or audio clips from smart TVs and transmits them to remote servers, where the data is utilized for measuring content viewership and delivering targeted advertisements.

The paper, titled "Watching the Watchers: Privacy Analysis of US Smart TV Automatic Content Recognition," analyzed eight smart TV operating systems across 12 devices from 10 manufacturers, including Amazon, Hisense, LG, Roku, Samsung, Sony, Supersonic, TCL, Vizio, and Westinghouse. The investigation focused on determining when these devices employ ACR and assessing the effectiveness of user opt-out mechanisms.
summary: Research from Northeastern University found that smart TVs from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue sending data to automatic content recognition endpoints after users opt out of tracking. The study examined eight smart TV operating systems across 12 devices from 10 manufacturers to assess the effectiveness of user tracking opt-outs.
author: Ars Technica

title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades
content:
BioWare, the renowned developer behind franchises such as Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Neverwinter Nights, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, has announced its closure. In a statement posted to social media on Wednesday afternoon, the studio confirmed that it is shutting down after more than three decades of operation. The announcement also revealed that early development on the next Mass Effect project will be terminated.

This decision followed a Bloomberg report published minutes earlier, which detailed 400 job cuts across Electronic Arts, BioWare’s parent company. The report, citing a person familiar with the company’s plans, specified that 50 positions at BioWare were affected by the layoffs.

In a message to staff, EA executives stated that the company is making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where they see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth. This strategic realignment spans EA’s entire portfolio as the company navigates its restructuring efforts.
summary: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon blocks AI agents while Walmart enables AI shopping with spending controls
content: Walmart is introducing new technology that allows AI agents to make purchases on customers' behalf, including controls for spending and transaction approvals. This strategy contrasts with Amazon, which is currently blocking AI agents from shopping on its site.
summary: Amazon is blocking AI agents from shopping on its site, while Walmart is introducing technology that allows AI agents to make purchases on customers' behalf. Walmart's new system includes controls for spending limits and transaction approvals.
author: TechCrunch

title: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
content: GM plans to debut a new central computer and electrical architecture on its fourth-generation EV platform in 2028, starting with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company states this technology is intended to help it compete with Tesla, Rivian, and various Chinese automakers.
summary: To compete with Tesla, Rivian, and a host of Chinese automakers, GM’s fourth-gen EV platform will roll out a new central computer and electrical architecture that will debut in 2028 in the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
author: TechCrunch

title: Automattic begins layoffs following board upheaval and executive departures
content: Automattic has initiated layoffs affecting multiple teams, including WordPress.com and its enterprise division, following a recent board shakeup and several executive departures. According to sources, the company may implement additional cuts as it seeks to improve its financial position.
summary: Automattic has begun laying off employees across multiple teams, including WordPress. Com and its enterprise business, following a board shakeup and a series of executive departures.
author: TechCrunch

title: Recursive releases Flint, a laptop coding model built largely by AI
content: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model. The company states the model was largely built by its own AI research system, serving as an early test of AI that improves itself.
summary: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system. The release is an early test of AI that improves itself.
author: TechCrunch

title: Russian drone attack kills two in Kyiv, residents inspect damaged homes
content: A Russian drone attack on Kyiv caused a fire in a residential building, killing two people. Residents returned to their homes to find debris and destroyed cars scattered around the damaged area. The incident left significant structural damage and a visible trail of wreckage.
summary: Two people were killed after a Russian drone attack sparked a fire in a residential building in Kyiv. Residents returned to damaged homes amid debris and destroyed cars littering the area.
author: Euronews

title: Canadian publisher drops Thélyson Orélien after confirming AI use in debut novel
content: A Canadian publisher announced on Wednesday that it has dropped Thélyson Orélien, a prize-nominated writer. The decision follows new information confirming that Orélien used artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut novel.
summary: A Canadian publisher dropped prize-nominated writer Thélyson Orélien on Wednesday. This decision followed new information indicating he used artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut novel.
author: France 24

title: Trump faces new scrutiny over ties to Putin labeled “humanitarian”
content:
US President Donald Trump’s shift in focus away from Ukraine has raised new questions regarding his relationship with Russian leader Vladimir Putin. A top American envoy described Putin as a "humanitarian" on Wednesday, highlighting the complex nature of the US-Russia dynamic.

Trump has framed his interactions with Putin as part of a comprehensive agreement that resulted in the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard. According to Trump, this deal is also intended to conclude Russia’s war on Ukraine.
summary: US President Donald Trump’s shift away from Ukraine has sparked fresh questions about his attachment to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, whom a top American envoy called a “humanitarian.” Trump says his dealings with Putin are part of a mega‑deal that secured the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard and will end Russia’s war on Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Le Pen to launch campaign as polls show wide first-round lead
content:
Marine Le Pen will officially launch her presidential campaign this weekend at a two‑day National Rally congress in Orléans.  

The latest Ifop poll, conducted after mass protests and riots in France, indicates that Le Pen would win the first round of the presidential election by a wide margin.  

The poll also shows far‑left candidate Jean‑Luc Melenchon as the most likely opponent in a potential runoff.  FRANCE 24’s Emerald Maxwell reports.
summary: Marine Le Pen will officially launch her presidential campaign at the National Rally congress in Orléans this weekend. A recent Ifop poll indicates she would win the first round by a wide margin, with Jean-Luc Melenchon as her likely opponent in the runoff.
author: France 24

title: Sudanese Army Drone Strike on Abyei Market Kills 153
content:
The death toll from a drone strike on the Amiet market in Abyei district, an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan, has risen to 153, with local authorities indicating the figure is likely higher. A local official told AFP on Wednesday that the strike, which occurred on Monday, involved multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army.

In a discussion with FRANCE 24’s Mark Owen, Jan Pospisil, a Sudan Affairs Analyst at the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform, commented on the incident. Pospisil noted that the Sudanese army has long attempted to portray itself as humane on the international stage while characterizing the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as committing atrocities. He stated that the recent attack clearly demonstrates that there is not much difference between the two groups, adding that neither the Sudanese military nor the RSF shows any acknowledgement of human life in the conflict.
summary: A drone strike on the Amiet market in Abyei district killed 153 people, authorities say. The strike, carried out by the Sudanese army using multiple munitions, was reported by a local official to AFP and the death toll is likely higher.
author: France 24

title: Trump uses France riots to push false immigration claims before midterms
content: Donald Trump and his inner circle are utilizing unrest in France to promote unsubstantiated claims that attribute the riots to immigration, a strategy that includes displaying French protest footage at midterm rallies. Despite the lack of evidence linking immigration to the disturbances, French President Emmanuel Macron has accused world leaders of making “stupid comments” at France’s expense. This political maneuvering occurs as Republicans face increasing pressure ahead of the midterms, coinciding with Trump’s approval rating reaching a reported record low.
summary: Trump uses France riots to push false immigration claims before midterms.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine supports US proposal for urgent three‑way talks with Russia and the United States
content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Wednesday that Ukraine supports a U.S. proposal for three‑way talks with Russia and the United States at the level of negotiators. He added that the talks should take place as soon as possible, preferably no later than early November.  

In an interview with FRANCE 24, Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House, noted that it is unclear whether Russian President Vladimir Putin would meet U.S. President Donald Trump and President Zelenskiy. Roos added that meeting Zelenskiy is the last thing Putin would be prepared to do.
summary: Ukraine supports US proposal for urgent three‑way talks with Russia and the United States.
author: France 24

content: Authorities searched the Patriots’ European Parliament offices as part of a long‑running funding inquiry. The group says the charges relate to its predecessor and that there is no legal continuity between the two.

title: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney conducts plant genetics experiments on ISS
content:
NASA astronaut Luke Delaney is conducting botany experiments aboard the International Space Station (ISS). The snapshot that appeared in the Space Photo of the Day for October 21, 2026 was captured by NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins, commander of SpaceX’s Crew‑13 mission to the ISS. In the image Delaney is seen working with petri dishes and experiment modules inside the station’s laboratory, while orbiting Earth in a vacuum of space.

Delaney’s work focuses on how plants respond to the microgravity environment. The experiments he is operating investigate the genetic responses of plants in this unique setting. By studying these genetic changes, scientists hope to better understand how plants grow when gravity is absent.

This is not the first time ISS astronauts have studied plants. Over the years, astronauts have grown peppers and other edible produce aboard the station, and have even demonstrated that moss can survive outside the ISS in the harsh environment of space. These studies form part of a broader program of biological research conducted on the station.

The ISS hosts a wide variety of life‑science experiments, from plants and animals to microscopic organisms. The data collected support human health, medical care, and Earth‑observing missions that monitor changing landforms, wildlife migration, glaciers, and natural disasters. While space remains the final frontier, the work done aboard the ISS is designed to benefit life on Earth.
summary: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney is conducting botany experiments aboard the International Space Station. The experiments, photographed by astronaut Jessica Watkins of SpaceX Crew‑13, study the genetic responses of plants in microgravity.

title: Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE review: Sharp astrophotography lens costs $464
content:
The Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE is a full-frame prime lens designed for Sony FE and Nikon Z mounts, released in May 2023. Priced at $464 (£533), the lens is positioned as a cost-effective option for astrophotography, offering a wide-angle field of view and a fast maximum aperture. It features an all-metal body with weather-sealing, weighing 19.4 oz (550 g) and measuring 3.35 x 4.06 inches (85.2 x 103 mm). The optical construction consists of 15 elements in 12 groups, including four ED glass and three aspherical lenses, designed to deliver sharpness and high contrast with minimal distortion.

In terms of image quality, the lens performs well for night photography, with testing indicating that ISO 800 was often sufficient for correct exposure under a moonless sky. Sharpness is excellent across the frame, including the corners, even when shooting wide open at f/1.8. While vignetting is strongest at f/1.8, it reduces significantly at f/2.8 and disappears entirely by f/4. A lens profile available in Adobe Camera Raw and Lightroom completely removes this vignetting. The lens exhibits only minimal chromatic aberration and a small amount of barrel distortion. Sharpness peaks at f/8, with slight drops at f/11 and further softening due to diffraction at f/16 and f/22, though the latter apertures are noted as less relevant for astrophotography.

Functionally, the lens offers a 105.6-degree field of view on full-frame sensors, equating to a 24mm focal length on APS-C cameras. It features internal focusing, which prevents the front element from rotating or extending, making it suitable for use with filters. The lens includes a manual focusing ring wide enough for glove use, a manual aperture ring with stepped or stepless operation, two customizable Fn buttons, and an AF/MF switch. A distinctive feature is a small, illuminated color digital screen on the top of the lens that displays focus distance, aperture settings, and active Fn controls.

Additional functionality includes a USB-C port on the lens mount for power and a Bluetooth connection to the Viltrox Lens app. This app allows users to update firmware and customize the Fn buttons and the digital screen’s welcome interface. The lens has a 77 mm filter thread and a minimum focusing distance of 10.6 inches (27 cm). Autofocus is driven by an SMT stepping motor, which locks onto subjects in approximately 0.25 seconds when wide open and 0.5 seconds when stopped down.

User reviews cited in the source highlight the lens’s value, image quality, and robust build. The review concludes that the lens represents excellent value for money, balancing professional-quality build and image performance with a mid-range price. It is recommended for users seeking a wide-angle prime for astrophotography, particularly those on a budget or planning to move from APS-C to full-frame formats. The package includes the lens, a lens hood, front and rear caps, and a soft lens case.
summary: Viltrox AF 16mm f/1.8 FE review: Sharp astrophotography lens costs $464.

title: ‘He had this electrical charge’: the short life and long legacy of Jason Molina, master of Americana
content: As a documentary celebrates the late US musician, friends and collaborators describe an incomparable storyteller who brought ‘myth and magic to everyday life’ Jason Molina grew up in a trailer in the working-class city of Lorain, Ohio. The city’s skyline once flickered with blue flames and a warm orange glow emanated from clattering steel mills, but by Molina’s teenage years, Lorain was in a tailspin. “Things were really on the economic decline,” says Tommy Nickoloff, Molina’s childhood friend and director of a new documentary: You Fuckers Figure It Out: A Jason Molina Story. “Nobody had any money and we were encouraged to get out. It’s a place where the American dream was born and died. And we watched it die.” Molina did indeed get out: the singer-songwriter released almost 20 studio albums and numerous EPs, primarily under the monikers Songs: Ohia and Magnolia Electric Co, spanning lo-fi to slowcore via polished Americana and alt-country. By 2009, he estimated he had written thousands of songs. But he died in 2013, aged 39, after years of alcoholism.
summary: ‘He had this electrical charge’: the short life and long legacy of Jason Molina, master of Americana.

title: Australia Collapse Leaves South Africa Near Victory
content:
Australia suffered a significant batting collapse in Gqeberha, being dismissed for 99 in their first innings and forced to follow on during the second Test against South Africa. This defeat came just one day after the home team scored over 400. The Australian team is now chasing a target while sitting at 156 for four, still trailing by 170 runs on the final day of the match.

The article describes the incident as another entry in Australia’s history of poor performances against South Africa, referencing previous low scores of 47 in Cape Town in 2011 and 85 in Hobart in 2016. The collapse was characterized by a rapid loss of wickets, with nine Australian batters falling in 38.3 overs. Notably, Nic Maddinson was dismissed in his first innings after facing only four balls on the third evening, before being out again an hour after lunch the following day.

South African bowlers Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada were highlighted for their aggressive spells, which involved high-speed deliveries that induced edges. Despite the batting failure leaving the door open for a South African victory, Australia retains a slim chance of saving the match on the final day.
summary: Australia were all out for 99 in Gqeberha after a 400+ home team score, leaving them 170 behind. The collapse, which included Nic Maddinson’s four‑ball first innings and nine wickets falling in 38.3 overs bowled by Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada, left South Africa close to victory.

title: HIV remnants in BACH2 gene may promote viral persistence by altering CD4 T cells
content:
New research from the Leibniz Institute of Virology (LIV) in Hamburg indicates that HIV genetic remnants can alter immune cells, potentially promoting viral persistence. While antiretroviral therapy suppresses the virus, its genetic material remains in the body. The study suggests that when HIV integrates into specific genes, such as the BACH2 master regulator, it changes the biology of the host cell.

This integration pushes CD4 T cells toward a state characterized by long-term survival, continued division, and altered immune activity. These changes imply that viral remnants do more than simply linger, actively influencing the behavior of the cells that carry them.
summary: Research from the Leibniz Institute of Virology indicates that HIV genetic remnants integrated into specific genes like BACH2 can change the biology of the host cell. content:

This spike in yields reflects growing anxiety in financial markets, which were further unsettled by recent violent street protests that left some civic buildings smouldering.

title: Some climate damage is now unavoidable even if we clean up our act
content:
The United Nations has acknowledged that limiting global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels will likely require an "overshoot, peak, decline" strategy, where temperatures exceed the threshold before cooling back down by 2100. This development highlights the critical question of whether climate damage is reversible. While scientists are racing to determine the extent of lasting harm, the situation presents a mix of potential recovery and irreversible loss.

Some positive indicators exist regarding the resilience of certain systems. Important land carbon sinks, such as the Amazon rainforest, appear capable of recovering from short-term climate shocks. Additionally, there is a possibility of resuscitating the AMOC, a vital ocean current, following a climate-induced collapse, although the process is described as difficult.

However, significant portions of climate impact are now locked in, regardless of immediate emission reductions. The Thwaites glacier in Antarctica is considered beyond saving even if ocean-driven melting were to stop immediately. Consequently, substantial future sea-level rise is inevitable. While this outcome is not a reason for despair, it underscores that passing the 1.5°C mark will leave lasting scars. The text emphasizes that while global cooling may eventually be achieved, the overshoot years will not be unscathed, making current emission cuts essential for the future.

title: NASA’s CASALS Lidar Fills Gaps in Earth’s 3D Surface Mapping
content:
NASA researchers at the Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) have developed the Concurrent Artificially-intelligent Spectrometry Lidar System (CASALS) to address significant gaps in current space-based laser measurements of Earth’s surface. Existing orbital instruments measure forests and terrain in narrow lines, leaving millions of acres unmapped between these tracks. Built with support from NASA’s Earth Science Technology Office (ESTO), CASALS blends machine learning with an ultra-compact lidar to create continuous, three-dimensional topographical renderings. The instrument’s primary innovation is its non-mechanical steering method, which uses light wavelength rather than moving mirrors to generate a continuous swath of data.

John Yorks, a physical research scientist at GSFC and Principal Investigator for CASALS, explained that the system utilizes a fast-pulsing, tunable “seed” laser centered at 1040 nanometers. This laser rapidly cycles through 256 unique wavelengths as it passes through a transmission grating, an optical component featuring a microscopic pattern of ridges. Due to the physics of diffraction, the grating bends light at slightly different angles based on its exact wavelength, naturally steering each of the 256 pulses into distinct positions across the flight path. This approach eliminates the need for heavy, failure-prone motorized mirrors, drastically reducing the instrument’s size, weight, and power requirements while enhancing reliability for the space environment.

A second key innovation is the detector array, which operates at an 80% Quantum Efficiency (QE). This high efficiency allows the instrument to convert incoming photons into electrical signals with minimal loss, enabling CASALS to detect weaker return signals from darker surfaces or through dense vegetation. In November 2024, an airborne prototype of CASALS flew aboard NASA’s B200 King Air aircraft, producing science-quality datasets on its first campaign. During a flight over the Great Cypress Swamp in Delaware, the instrument captured detailed imagery showing tree canopy tops in green, the ground in purple, and near-ground vegetation in blue.

Yorks noted that the instrument performed well from its first flight, exceeding team expectations. Flying at an altitude of roughly five kilometers, CASALS achieved a 22-centimeter horizontal resolution, allowing it to distinguish individual tree branches and subtle changes in ground elevation. Yorks stated that the system provides fine details of vegetation structure and surface topography. The team is currently preparing for further development, with plans to widen the instrument’s swath and add onboard data processing software before creating a space-ready prototype.

The next scheduled flight for the airborne prototype is planned for summer 2027 as part of the Airborne Surface, Cryosphere, Ecosystem, and Nearshore Topography (ASCENT) campaign. The project is supported by NASA’s Decadal Survey Incubation (DSI) program, NASA’s Instrument Incubation Program (IIP), NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University. If successful, CASALS could become the first spaceborne lidar capable of mapping Earth’s forests and terrain as continuous three-dimensional swaths rather than isolated profiles.
summary: NASA’s CASALS instrument uses wavelength steering to create continuous 3D swaths, filling the gaps left by traditional line‑by‑line lidar. An airborne prototype flew aboard a B200 King Air in November 2024, producing science‑quality data and demonstrating the system’s performance at 22‑centimeter resolution.

title: Perseverance rover drives 45.22 km, longest distance on another celestial body
content:
NASA’s Perseverance rover has established a new record for the farthest distance driven on another celestial body. On Sol 2006, which corresponds to October 11, 2026, the rover’s odometer reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles). To celebrate this achievement, the rover’s engineering twin on Earth received a plaque from Guinness World Records. The milestone was documented by an image taken with the rover’s Left Navigation Camera at a local mean solar time of 14:40:39, showing the wheel tracks from the record-breaking drive.

The path to this record involved a period of intensive scientific activity. Approximately two months prior, on Sol 1947, the odometer was only about 200 meters from the milestone, a distance that could have been covered in a single drive using Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav). However, the rover remained in a scientifically significant area, utilizing short drives to perform rock abrasions and proximity science on ancient rock outcrops. When the rover eventually departed for a new site, it surpassed the distance record.

Achieving this distance required the engineering team to adapt to challenging Martian terrain, including dense boulder fields and steep slopes. Following thousands of simulations, the team adjusted the rover’s operational parameters to better handle tough conditions. These changes included raising the tilt limit to 24 degrees and reducing the required clearance under the rover’s belly pan to 20 centimeters (about 7.9 inches). Additionally, the team updated the braking software to avoid rock hazards, nearly doubled the steer motor current limits, and implemented “dynamic slip tables” in the flight software to model expected slip. The team also utilized cross-slope driving techniques to better anchor the wheels on exposed bedrock.

A significant technological advancement supporting these longer drives is the autonomous capability known as onboard Global Localization (GBLC). This system repurposes the high-speed commercial processor from the Ingenuity Helicopter Base Station to compare ground and orbital imagery, allowing the rover to autonomously determine its location in global coordinates at the end of a drive. This capability functions similarly to GPS, enabling Perseverance to travel longer distances without human intervention.

Because this commercial processor is not hardened against the radiation environment on Mars, the team developed a software-based approach to mitigate the effects of “transient bit flips” in memory. The lack of a global magnetosphere and a thin atmosphere on Mars provides little shielding from radiation. Looking ahead, the team is exploring the use of generative AI to help propose solutions for steering AutoNav along strategic paths, aiming to plan more activities with fewer resources as the rover continues to climb higher along the crater rim.
summary: Perseverance rover drives 45.22 km, longest distance on another celestial body.

title: The Download Launches Impossible Issue Spotlighting Lunar AI and Synthetic Blood
content:
MIT Technology Review has announced the release of its “Impossible” print issue, described as the final edition of 2026. The publication focuses on ambitious technological endeavors, including attempts to create synthetic blood, build lunar cities, and achieve cognitive immortality. The issue also investigates artificial intelligence’s capacity to refuse requests, bionic eyes that restore sight, and the development of blended meat. Additionally, it reviews six technologies that have long been anticipated but not yet realized. The editors state that the issue honors scientists and engineers who pursue daring projects to make life better, safer, and healthier.

A key story in the newsletter highlights Astrolab’s FLIP lunar rover, which is scheduled to launch to the moon as early as next month. The rover carries a computer capable of running large language models (LLMs), marking the first time such AI software will operate in a lunar environment. The mission aims to test whether LLMs can facilitate greater autonomy and real-time decision-making despite extreme temperatures and cosmic radiation.

Another featured article discusses research conducted in Alaska’s Denali National Park, where a 2013 lightning fire burned nearly 35,000 acres and removed the insulating layer that preserves permafrost. Scientists are using this event to study how fires impact permafrost and carbon storage. Their findings indicate that warming temperatures fuel fires, which cause permafrost to thaw and release greenhouse gases, creating a cascading feedback loop that accelerates further warming.

In the AI sector, the newsletter reports on a 26,000-word blog post by Nick Cammarata, a researcher at AI startup Goodfire. Cammarata claims that LLMs may be easier to understand, monitor, and control than previously thought. While the post has generated significant industry attention, the article notes that not everyone is convinced of these findings. MIT Technology Review interviewed Cammarata the day after the post was published to discuss his research and the skepticism surrounding it.

The newsletter also summarizes several other recent developments. Elon Musk reportedly ordered a recent Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, which hampered drone strikes and air defenses. Additionally, SpaceX and Tesla have begun merger discussions, with special committees formed to evaluate a potential deal that could combine their AI and manufacturing plans. Other reported news includes Ukraine carrying out the world’s first drone evacuation of a soldier, Meta pausing Muse sharing after private chats were exposed online, and more than 1,000 mathematicians pledging to avoid AI companies and tools.

The edition concludes with a segment on defense technology, specifically a high-powered microwave weapon developed by startup Epirus. The US armed forces are interested in this technology as a method to disable drones in large numbers. The device pushes out kilowatts of power to disrupt drone circuits, offering a cost-efficient alternative to traditional counter-drone measures.
summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Introducing: the Impossible issue We wanted our last print edition of 2026 to include a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas.

title: Samsung Odyssey G80HF 27‑inch 5K monitor sells for $599 with 180Hz gaming
content:
Samsung’s 27‑inch Odyssey G80HF 5K monitor is positioned as a budget‑friendly option for gamers who want a high‑resolution screen without breaking the bank. The model is available for $599.99 at Amazon and B&H Photo, a price that is $100 lower than its best listed price. The monitor’s Fast IPS panel can run in two modes: a 5K resolution at up to 180 Hz or a 1440p resolution at up to 360 Hz. Samsung advertises Nvidia G‑Sync compatibility and AMD FreeSync Premium support to keep the refresh rate synchronized with the graphics card’s output.

Connectivity on the G80HF includes a single DisplayPort 2.1 (bandwidth not specified), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub that offers two USB‑A 3.2 Gen 1 ports for charging or connecting accessories. One of the monitor’s highlighted features is its one‑millisecond response time, a specification that is common on lower‑priced gaming displays but less frequent on 5K monitors at this price point.

For comparison, LG’s 27‑inch UltraGear evo 5K Mini LED monitor sells for $799.99. It offers more dimming zones for a more accurate picture, a higher maximum brightness, and a USB‑C video input that can deliver 90 W of power to charge a device while it is in use. The UltraGear’s dual‑mode refresh rates are 165 Hz and 330 Hz, which are lower than the Samsung’s 180 Hz and 360 Hz options, but the article notes that this difference is not considered a major drawback.

Other promotions highlighted in the article include a Grand Theft Auto VI preorder bundle that gives a $10 discount on a gaming gift card when the game is added to a Best Buy bundle. The bundle also contains other titles such as Gears of War: E‑Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. The remake of Demon’s Souls is available on the PlayStation Store for $13.49 as a digital deluxe edition, with the sale ending on November 4th on the West Coast or 2:59 AM ET on November 5th on the East Coast. Additionally, Ugreen’s Nexode Pro multi‑port wall charger is listed at $59.99 on Amazon and Ugreen, offering up to 160 W of total power with four USB‑C ports (each up to 140 W when a single device is plugged in) and one USB‑A port. The charger features folding prongs and a rotating display.
summary: There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen.

title: Google launches Conversational Gemini navigation on Apple CarPlay
content:
Google has expanded its Gemini AI assistant, first launched on Android Auto last year, to Apple CarPlay. The conversational Gemini navigation feature is live today for drivers in the United States, and Google says a global rollout is also under way, though regional details have not been provided.

The update lets CarPlay users speak to the voice assistant within Google Maps for hands‑free assistance while driving. Users can ask multi‑step questions, such as for place recommendations and then request directions that avoid toll roads. Google noted the addition comes roughly 12 months after the Android Auto launch.
summary: Google launches Conversational Gemini navigation on Apple CarPlay.

title: Apple Music launches new logo, updated wordmark and sound in rebrand
content:
Apple announced a rebrand of Apple Music, unveiling a new logo, an updated wordmark and a fresh sound track. The redesign follows a redesigned wordmark shown in a video and an updated app icon that appeared in the iOS 27.2 beta. The new sound was created by British producer Fred Again in collaboration with Nest Acoustics.

In a promotional video, Apple explains that the rebrand “wanted sound to create the visuals,” featuring the music‑note logo and wordmark submerged in water that reacts to the audio. The video demonstrates the water‑based animation of the new visual identity.
summary: Apple officially introduced a rebrand of Apple Music with a new logo, updated wordmark and a new sound. The new sound was composed by British producer Fred Again and Nest Acoustics and was shown in a video and an iOS 27.2 beta app icon.

title: Supernatural VR fitness game relaunches with Early Access on Meta Horizon Store
content:
Supernatural, the fitness VR game previously supported by Meta, has relaunched as an independent app with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store. The new version launches today with thousands of “remastered” workouts and a selection of new routines, and additional content is slated for release.

summary: Supernatural, a fitness VR game, has relaunched with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store, offering thousands of remastered workouts and some new ones starting today. title: EA shuts down BioWare studio and cancels upcoming Mass Effect game
content:
Electronic Arts confirmed that BioWare, the studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, is shutting down. In an internal announcement, EA also said it will not continue development of the next Mass Effect game that was in progress. The company is laying off roughly 400 staff members, Bloomberg reports.

The shutdown comes after EA completed a $55 billion privatization deal in August. “BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role‑playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” said Cam Weber, EA president.
summary: BioWare is shutting down and EA announced it will not continue development on the next Mass Effect game that was in the works. The closure includes laying off around 400 staffers and comes after EA went private in a $55 billion deal that closed in August.

content: Blacksmith, a platform that enables companies to build and test AI code more effectively, announced a $66 million Series C financing round led by Sequoia. The investment values Blacksmith at $1 billion, giving the company unicorn status.

title: Modern Warfare 4 praised for narrative-driven campaign set in South Korea invasion
content:
Modern Warfare 4’s campaign has been highlighted for its narrative focus, positioning character and consequence at the core of its large‑scale battles. The game’s story unfolds during an invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbour, featuring a fictional authoritarian regime led by a new ruler who deploys a powerful experimental weapon as the opening move of the attack.

Players assume the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier. Alongside a small unit of similarly inexperienced grunts, Jun is thrust into a firestorm of burning cities and enemy paratroopers. The setting and storytelling have drawn praise, with some writers suggesting the campaign may rank among the best Call of Duty single‑player experiences in at least six years.
summary: The upcoming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign is being hailed as the series' strongest in at least six years. It places players in the role of Park Hyun Jun, a conscripted South Korean soldier caught in a fictional invasion of South Korea by its northern neighbor.

content:

The article notes that the lineup now includes options with colour screens, devices designed for note‑taking, and child‑friendly versions, alongside models aimed at tighter budgets.

content:
Poland’s lower house of parliament approved two bills that would loosen the country’s near‑total abortion ban.  Campaigners describe the move as a “small‑scale step” and say it comes amid protests demanding the government follow through on promises to overhaul abortion laws.

The new measures would remove some criminal penalties for people who help women access abortion care and would allow terminations in cases of fetal abnormalities.  Officials say the bills are likely to be vetoed by President Jarosław Kaczyński.
summary: Poland’s lower house of parliament approved two bills to loosen the near‑total abortion ban. The measures would cut penalties for those helping women obtain abortions and allow terminations for fetal abnormalities, but are expected to be vetoed by the nationalist president.

content:

title: Shark named Bukang-i freed after month trapped in Busan canal

Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i. On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.
summary: South Korea’s oceans ministry said the shark, affectionately known as Bukang-i, was successfully guided out of the Busan canal after more than a month trapped. content: Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’ The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday. title: New book details 1949 meeting between Langston Hughes and Nina Simone
content: A new book charts how a 1949 meeting between the renowned poet and the legendary musician, then a 16-year-old girl, sparked enduring ties and fruitful collaboration In 1949, the poet and writer Langston Hughes was already a towering figure – he toured the country reading his poems and lecturing, drawing crowds that filled auditoriums. That year, at a lecture in Asheville, North Carolina, Hughes met a 16-year-old girl, Eunice Waymon, who would go on to make history in her own right using her stage name, Nina Simone. Hughes and Simone became friends and collaborators, working together on songs such as Backlash Blues, which soundtracked what was then a nascent Black Power movement. The song influenced Kwame Ture, the activist and Black revolutionary who was then known as Stokely Carmichael, who popularized the phrase “Black power”.
summary: A new book charts how a 1949 meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, between poet Langston Hughes and 16-year-old Eunice Waymon sparked an enduring friendship. The two collaborated on songs such as Backlash Blues, which influenced activist Stokely Carmichael.

title: Thure Erik Lund's 'The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch' translated into English
content: Translated into English at last, this portrait of a man appalled by modernity and desperate to get back to nature is brimming with Nordic weltschmerz T-O-M. The initials of Tomas Olsen Myrbråten, the narrator in Thure Erik Lund’s The Mystery of What Befell in the Ditch, spell out the Norwegian word for “empty”. Approaching 38, he’s already a relic. He spends his days slumped at the kitchen table or staring out of the window, convinced that the ceiling is about to fall and crush him. He sobs about the state he’s in and the state of society around him. Of one thing he’s sure: “It is no longer me who cries, but the world, the world crying, in me.” Nordic weltschmerz: you’d have to be a saint not to giggle. Lund has been described by Karl Ove Knausgård as the “greatest Norwegian contemporary writer”; this novel, originally published in 1999, is his first to be translated into English. In it, Tomas describes himself, over and over and over again, as a “life-of-the-mind individual”. Cursed as much as blessed, life-of-the mind individuals have a keen and unconsoling sense of how things are (“one is a wretched, contemptible, and unworthy being”) and how things will end for them (“in the sewers of society, at nature’s nadir, incessantly ground down into the mud and the mire so that one day, millions of years from now, they become oil, life-of-the-mind oil, at the very bottom of life itself”). Is he making fun of himself? In 2026, he seems closer to an eco-prophet.
summary: This novel, originally published in 1999, is the first work by Thure Erik Lund to be translated into English. The book features a narrator named Tomas Olsen Myrbråten who is described as a "life-of-the-mind individual" appalled by modernity.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Coach banned until 2048 for training DR Congo kids while suspended for sexual abuse
content:
Jonathan Bukabakwa, a coach in the Democratic Republic of the Congo known as Messi, has had his Fifa ban extended by five years until 2048. The world governing body imposed the additional penalty after the Guardian revealed that Bukabakwa continued to train young players despite being suspended for the sexual abuse of a minor. He had previously received a 20-year ban from football.

In addition to the extended ban, Bukabakwa was ordered to pay a $15,000 (£11,200) fine. The DRC’s Football Association was also ordered to improve its education and compliance measures.
summary: Coach banned until 2048 for training DR Congo kids while suspended for sexual abuse.

title: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to have surgery after ACL rupture, PSG's most serious injury
content:
Paris Saint-Germain’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Tuesday’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Barcelona. The Georgian player twisted his knee just before the hour mark and was helped off the pitch, unable to put any weight on his right leg.

This injury is the most serious of three sustained by PSG, as Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos are also out for weeks.
summary: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during Paris Saint‑Germain’s 4‑2 Champions League win over Barcelona. His injury is the most serious of three PSG injuries, with Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos also out for weeks.

title: Gary Neville's The Overlap goes daily as Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart join
content:
Gary Neville’s podcast, The Overlap, has transitioned to a daily format, reflecting the creator’s expanding media presence. Recent additions to the show include former footballers Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart, joining a growing roster of guests. This expansion occurs against a backdrop where former footballers are increasingly entering the creator economy, with many establishing podcasts or YouTube channels.

The article notes that while other former players like Gary Lineker have diversified their content, The Overlap largely remains focused on football. Although a rugby podcast associated with the brand was discontinued in February, a cricket equivalent continues to operate. The piece positions Neville’s media empire as a dominant force in this sector, distinguishing it from the broader, more varied agenda of rival productions.
summary: The Overlap has transitioned to a daily format with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to the podcast family. The content primarily focuses on football, while a rugby podcast was mothballed in February and a cricket equivalent continues.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Philipp Lahm: Manchester City's rule-breaking deserves punishment
content: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri.
summary: Philipp Lahm states that while Manchester City achieved greatness, their rule-breaking behavior deserves to be punished. He also notes that the Bundesliga's member-controlled structure can show the way forward for football.

title: Chris Woakes publishes autobiography The Wizard
content: All-rounder and ‘the best teammate you could wish for’ has seen profound change since his first-class debut in 2006 The Spin this week comes from York, where Chris Woakes and I sat down on Monday evening to discuss his new autobiography, The Wizard. There were just shy of 400 international wickets on stage, not a single one mine, and an audience that happened to include one of his old teachers. It turns out a seemingly clean-cut cricketer was something of a rebel back in the day, with Mr Wager reminding Chris of the time he feigned illness to bunk off school for a long weekend in Newquay with his mates. A bit like Warwickshire’s title win this year that anecdote came too late, frustratingly, for the hardback edition.
summary: Chris Woakes released his new autobiography, The Wizard, and discussed it in York. The book details his life as an all-rounder and teammate since his first-class debut in 2006.

title: Antonelli's first F1 title and Mercedes upgrades in focus at Austin GP
content:
Kimi Antonelli is poised to secure his maiden Formula 1 world championship at the United States Grand Prix in Austin this weekend. The young Italian driver’s title is described as all but secured, marking the culmination of a childhood dream. The event is expected to bring intense media attention as Antonelli attempts to seal his first championship.

While the driver’s primary focus is on winning the title, his Mercedes team faces significant scrutiny regarding performance. The outcome at the United States Grand Prix will provide crucial insights into Mercedes’ upgrades, which will inform the team’s strategy and competitiveness as they prepare for next season’s championship run.
summary: Kimi Antonelli is poised to secure his maiden championship at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Mercedes will also use the event to assess performance upgrades that will inform their strategy for next season.

title: Jonas Eidevall says San Diego Wave eye title as they sit second in NWSL
content: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is reveling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the NWSL, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.”
summary: Former Arsenal head coach Jonas Eidevall leads San Diego Wave, who are second in the NWSL, one point behind the leader with two matches before the playoffs. The team is on a five‑game winning streak and Eidevall says they can go all the way and are targeting silverware.

content: President Trump announced on Wednesday that Russia has released imprisoned American teacher Stephen Hubbard. title: UK approves Jackdaw gasfield, bringing relief to Aberdeen workers
content:
The UK has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, a decision that has brought relief to Aberdeen despite limited expectations for a return to past economic highs. While few believe the approval will restore the city to its previous boom years, local workers hope it will secure North Sea jobs for the time being. The development is seen as a stabilizing factor for the region’s economy, with some residents noting that the project helps them pay their mortgages.

Aberdeen’s current economic landscape contrasts sharply with its history. In 2012, the city boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK, a status bolstered by an ATM reportedly having the highest withdrawal rate in Europe during the 1990s. During that era, fossil fuel firms transformed the city’s grand granite houses into company offices, and house prices skyrocketed as workers scrambled for space.

However, the city has experienced a significant reversal since the 2014 oil price shock. Today, “for sale” and “to let” signs are common on Aberdeen’s main thoroughfares. Disposable income in the city has fallen by nearly 20% between 2013 and 2023, a decline that is more severe than in any other large UK city.
summary: The UK has approved the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea, providing relief for workers hoping to secure local employment. Although few believe the decision will restore Aberdeen’s past boom years, the city has experienced a significant decline in disposable income since 2013.

In the late 1990s, Hillman predicted that future generations would question the actions taken by their predecessors to prevent global climate catastrophe. This foresight was echoed two decades later when Greta Thunberg addressed the United Nations, stating that young people were beginning to understand the betrayal of the current generation and that the eyes of future generations were upon them.

Additionally, Hillman warned twenty-five years ago that public denial of the climate crisis would only begin to crack when people in the global north were personally affected. He cited specific scenarios for this shift, including the creation of millions of environmental refugees from uninhabitable regions or instances where homes were flooded repeatedly, making them uninsurable. His work highlighted the connection between direct personal impact and the breakdown of public denial regarding environmental issues.

title: Chlamydomonas alga and channelrhodopsin illuminate brain memory mechanisms

Chlamydomonas swims toward light by means of a protein named channelrhodopsin. This protein is remarkably similar to the rhodopsin found in human eyes.

When channelrhodopsin detects light, electrically charged ions rush into the cell from outside. The influx triggers an extremely fast electrical signal that directs the alga’s hair‑like motor to move.
summary: Researchers used the one-celled alga Chlamydomonas, which swims toward light via the protein channelrhodopsin, to study how memories, feelings and behaviour form in the brain.
